topic: Tests of adequacy of index numbers
question: Explain the tests used to check the adequacy of an index number formula. Which of these tests does Fisher's ideal index satisfy?
sources: Index numbers: tests of adequacy (standard statistical principles)

points.label: Unit test
points.description: The formula should give a result that does not depend on the units in which prices or quantities are quoted; all common formulas except the simple aggregative index satisfy it.

points.label: Time reversal test
points.description: If the base and current periods are interchanged, the two indices should be reciprocals: P01 × P10 = 1 (ignoring the factor 100).

points.label: Factor reversal test
points.description: If price and quantity are interchanged, the product of the price index and the quantity index should equal the value index: P01 × Q01 = V01.

points.label: Circular test
points.description: An index should work in a chain so that P01 × P12 × P20 = 1; it is satisfied by the simple geometric mean of price relatives and by a fixed-weight aggregative index.

points.label: Fisher's ideal index
points.description: Fisher's index, the geometric mean of the Laspeyres and Paasche indices, satisfies the unit, time reversal and factor reversal tests but not the circular test, which is why it is called ideal.
